blocks.text: **The problem.** Given a string `s`, return the length of the **longest substring** (consecutive characters) in which **no character repeats**.

blocks.alt: In abcabcbb the longest substring without a repeat is abc, length 3. In pwwkew it is wke, length 3 — pwke is not a substring, because its letters are not next to each other.

blocks.text: Try every substring and test whether all its characters are different — a set of its characters is exactly as big as the substring when nothing repeats.
**Time O(n³), space O(min(n, σ))**, where σ is the size of the alphabet.
2. Optimal: a sliding window with a set

Keep a **window** `s[left..right]` with no repeats, and a set of the characters inside it. Move `right` one step at a time. If the new character is already in the set, shrink from the left — removing characters one by one — until its old copy is gone. Every window you see is repeat-free, and both ends only ever move forward.

blocks.alt: pwwkew: the window grows to pw. At index 2 the second w is already in the window, so left moves past the first w to index 2. The window grows to wke, length 3, then the last w repeats and left moves past the w at index 2.

elements.text: left jumps past the first w: 0 -> 2
elements.originalText: left jumps past the first w: 0 -> 2

blocks.text: **Time O(n)** — each character enters and leaves the window at most once, so about 2n steps — **space O(min(n, σ)).**
3. Best solution: remember the last index, and jump

Removing characters one by one is wasted work: we already know where the repeat's old copy is. Keep a map **character → last index seen**. When `s[right]` was last seen at an index **inside** the window, jump `left` straight to that index + 1. If it was seen **before** `left`, it's an old copy that no longer matters — ignore it.

blocks.alt: abba: at index 2 the second b was last seen at index 1, inside the window, so left jumps to 2. At index 3, a was last seen at index 0 — but 0 is left of left = 2, outside the window, so it is ignored. The window becomes ba, length 2.

blocks.caption: L and R mark the window; the map keeps each character's last index.

blocks.text: **Time O(n)** — exactly one step per character — **space O(min(n, σ)).** The `>= left` check is the one people forget; without it, "abba" would move `left` *backwards* to 1 and report 3.

items: **An old copy outside the window** — `"abba"`: 2. Needs the `last[ch] >= left` check.
**Spaces and symbols count as characters** — `" "`: 1; `"a b"`: 3.
**Longest Substring with At Most Two Distinct Characters** (and *at most K*) — allow repeats, but cap the number of kinds: a map of counts. That's the next lesson.
**Longest Repeating Character Replacement** — replace at most k characters to make the longest run of one letter.
**Maximum Erasure Value** — the same window over numbers, maximising the sum instead of the length.
**Count substrings without repeating characters** — at each right end, every start from `left` to `right` works: add `right − left + 1`.
